title: Protocol category menu (Device Info/WiFi/BT/GPS/System)
description: Restructure the flat 38-item main menu into top-level protocol categories. New top-level Submenu scene (Device Info, WiFi, Bluetooth, GPS, System); reuse scene_start as the per-category VariableItemList renderer filtered by item.category. Split composite Attack/Sniff into WiFi+BT variants; tag every item with MMMenuCategory. BT section probes once (sniffbt -> 'Bluetooth not supported') and greys when unsupported. Scripts/Save routing converted from index NUM-2/-1 to name-based. See plan snug-plotting-dragonfly.
notes: Implemented: new top-level categories Submenu scene (Device Info/WiFi/Bluetooth/GPS/System) is the app root; scene_start repurposed as per-category renderer filtered by item.category with a display-row->flat-index map. items[] retagged (37 items); Attack->WiFi Attack+BT Spam, Sniff->WiFi Sniff+BT Sniff, Airtag->BT. Scripts/Save routing now name-based. BT probe: sniffbt on first top-menu render, greys 'Bluetooth (no HW)' on 'not supported' (mm_bt_line_unsupported, host-tested). Back in a category returns to categories; Back at categories exits app. settings-init prompt moved to categories (flag cleared by settings_init). Built clean API 87.1, all host tests pass. Untested on-device.
close_reason: Verified on-device: protocol category menu (Device Info/WiFi/BT/GPS/System) works; BT greys to '(no HW)' on the S2; WiFi/GPS/System sections and name-based Scripts/Save routing all function; fixed a launch NULL-deref by moving first-scene launch after UART init.

title: Host Scan: parse pingscan stream live; drop 45s wait
description: Host Scan found 0 hosts despite the laptop being on the network. Root cause: the scene waited a fixed ~45s then read list -i, but pingscan's slow sweep hadn't populated by 45s (captured over bridge: pingscan is slow to start, then STREAMS bare-IP host lines). The 45s window also discarded every streamed IP. Fix: parse the streamed pingscan IPs live into the host store (dedup, throttled rebuild), grow the list as found, no fixed cutoff, drop the list -i phase. New mm_pingscan_parse_ip parser rejects the IP/Gateway/Netmask/MAC header lines; host test added. Verified list -i format [n] ip was already correct.
notes: On-device: still returns 0 hosts after the streaming rewrite. Deferred. Next: use the ESP32 Marauder source (/Users/barbecuesteve/Code/ESP32Marauder) to check pingscan's actual output/behavior and whether it requires the ESP to be joined at scan time; verify the app was joined when Host Scan ran.

title: Live Scan: continuous scan, resolve targeting on AP select
description: Currently scanall runs a fixed ~10s then stops to run list -a/list -c (needed for select-index targeting), capping the AP list. Restructure: scanall runs continuously the whole time the user is on the Live view (list keeps growing); defer the resolve (stopscan + list -a + list -c) to the moment an AP is tapped, showing a brief 'Resolving...' state before the detail scene. Resume scanning (no clearlist) on return from detail. Rescan still does a clean clearlist restart. Fix cursor preservation to track by store index so the alphabetical sort stays stable as the list grows. Verified via A/B that ChanHop is irrelevant to scanall yield (see bd memory).
notes: Implemented (option A). scanall now runs continuously on the Live view (no 10s cap); AP tap triggers begin_resolve (stopscan -> list -a -> list -c -> 'Resolving...' ~3s) then opens detail. Return from detail resumes scanall without clearlist (store persists, keeps growing); on_exit to menu clears the store so re-entry is fresh; Rescan still does a clean clearlist restart. Live rebuild now sorts alphabetically with cursor preserved by STORE index so the sort stays stable as APs arrive. Built clean vs API 87.1. Awaiting on-device check.
close_reason: Implemented and verified on-device: continuous scan with resolve-on-tap works; tapping an AP resolves then opens detail, station list shows clients, station Fox Hunt works. Fixed a store-wipe regression: scene_manager_next_scene calls on_exit on forward push, so the on_exit store reset wiped stations the detail/list scenes needed. Replaced with a scan_resume_pending flag; on_exit no longer wipes.

title: Fox Hunt: staleness/waiting feedback for quiet stations
description: Station Fox Hunt is correct but its UX hides the quiet-station reality. (1) Replace the static 'Acquiring...' with a clearly-alive 'Waiting for TX...' state so a quiet station doesn't look hung. (2) Track time since last RSSI sample; when a station goes quiet, show the reading as stale (age, or dim/greyed) instead of freezing on a misleading number. (3) Optional one-line hint that clients only report when transmitting. Discovered while verifying mm-d5j.
notes: Implemented in fox_hunt.c: 'Waiting for TX...' state for a never-acquired station (AP still says 'Acquiring...'); tracks fox_last_rx_tick and shows 'stale Ns' once a reading ages past ~1.5s. Built clean vs API 87.1. Awaiting on-device confirm.
close_reason: Verified on-device: quiet station shows 'Waiting for TX...'; readings gain a 'stale Ns' marker when the station goes idle and clear when it resumes.

title: Confirm ViewPort lockup reduction holds under sustained load
description: Throttled rebuilds (2Hz), 4KB stream buffer, per-tick line cap (24) were added to stop GUI lockups in the live scan / beacon / probe monitors. Verify no lockups over a long scanall + beacon-mon session on hardware.
notes:
Added MM-PERF timing (Info, >=8ms only) around the 4 GUI-thread hot spots in scan_live: per-tick drain, submenu rebuild (with item count), list -a resolve burst, list -c parse+final rebuild. Goal: correlate which op's duration coincides with the ViewPort lockup warnings before optimizing.
MEASURED: every ViewPort lockup coincides 1:1 with an MM-PERF 'rebuild' line; drain/resolve/parse never crossed 8ms. Rebuild cost was ~8ms flat for n=6..16 -> it's view-model lock contention with the GUI draw thread, not per-item work. Fix: rebuild only when the AP set grows (prompt, ~2/s) instead of on every station-count change; station-only updates get a slow ~3s refresh; list -c still fills authoritative counts at scan end. Awaiting on-device re-measure.
FIX MEASURED on-device: rebuild-gating cut lockups from 6 to 1 per scan and rebuilds from ~9 to 2. The lone residual is a single new-AP rebuild occasionally contending the view-model lock (~8ms) -- inherent to the submenu public API, benign warning, GUI recovers. MM-PERF probes demoted to Debug. Committed. Leaving open pending a longer sustained-load soak to fully confirm it holds.

title: Verify multi-attack selection clearing on hardware
description: mm_select_target() deselects the previously-selected AP/station before selecting the new target, because Marauder 'select' toggles/accumulates. Confirm on hardware that firing deauth on AP B after AP A hits only B, not both.

title: Verify station Fox Hunt (foxhunt -s) on hardware
description: Confirm 'foxhunt -s <ap> <station>' from the station-detail scene produces a live RSSI meter that tracks the specific client. Only AP fox hunt (foxhunt -w) is hardware-confirmed so far.
notes: Added FURI_LOG instrumentation (tags MM-FOX, MM-TGT): logs foxhunt -s/-w args, capped raw ESP replies, and the exact indices behind any (not targetable) rejection. Built clean vs API 87.1. Debugging ~1/4 station foxhunt success rate reported on hardware.
close_reason: Verified on hardware: station foxhunt -s works. The apparent ~1/4 success rate was quiet stations, not a bug -- a client only yields RSSI when it transmits (unlike an AP's continuous beacons). Instrumentation (MM-FOX) confirmed correct args + RSSI stream once the station was active.

title: Device Info (Mate): parsed 'info' screen
description: New main-menu entry 'Device Info (Mate)' runs 'info' and renders the key:value fields (Firmware/Version/Hardware/ESP-IDF/Station MAC/AP MAC/SD Card/...) as a scrollable submenu instead of raw console. One-shot query: collect ~1.5s then render. Skips the #info echo and > prompt lines.
notes: Verified on-device: Device Info screen is perfect.
close_reason: Verified on-device: parsed Device Info screen works.

title: Auto-join from optional networks file on SD
description: Join action looks up the AP's SSID in /ext/apps_data/marauder/networks.txt (FlipperFormat: SSID/Pass pairs); on an exact match it sends 'join -a <idx> -p <pw>' straight to the console without a keyboard prompt (password never shown). No match or hidden AP falls back to typing on the Flipper. File is plaintext on unencrypted removable SD (user's own networks, user's own risk); gitignored, ships as networks.txt.example placeholders only; password handled in RAM, zeroed after use, never logged by our code. NOTE: Marauder echoes the password in its own join output, so a saved console log (if log-saving is on) will contain it -- same as the existing manual join.
notes:
Added save-back (per-join consent): after a typed join for a known SSID, a 'Save for later?' Yes/No dialog offers to store the password. On Yes, mm_save_network_password() upserts into networks.txt (replaces existing SSID entry or appends; whole-file rewrite via flipper_format; static buffers to avoid stack overflow). Consent is per-join, never silent. Success-detection deferred (still saves on submit, not confirmed connect) -- follow-up once Marauder join success/failure strings are captured. Built clean API 87.1. Untested on-device.
Fixed the save-prompt lockup: a blocking dialog_message_show from the text-input event handler deadlocks the fullscreen GUI loop (existing dialogs only run at startup). Replaced with a widget-button confirm scene (join_save), mirroring script_confirm_delete. Also added a clean Join result scene (wifi_marauder_scene_join): runs the join command and shows 'Joining <SSID>' + status/IP, SUPPRESSING Marauder's post-join settings dump -- which echoes the command and ClientPW, i.e. the plaintext password. mm_join_line_is_noise/parse_ip/classify parsers added with host tests (tools/join_parser_test.c) asserting no password-bearing line is ever displayable. All join paths (auto, typed+save, hidden) now route to the result scene instead of raw console. Built clean API 87.1; host tests green. Untested on-device.
close_reason: Shipped & verified on-device: auto-join reads networks.txt (FlipperFormat SSID/Pass), per-join 'Save for later?' confirm scene banks typed passwords, clean Join result screen shows Connecting/Connected/Failed while suppressing Marauder's settings dump (never displays the plaintext password), and a '* Connected (joined)' indicator marks the joined AP. Marauder has no disconnect command (only reboot), so indicator-only per user choice. Host tests cover the join parsers incl. password suppression.

title: Trim Fox Hunt debug logging before ship
description: The MM-FOX per-line rx logging (up to 40 FURI_LOG_I/launch) was added to diagnose mm-d5j and is now noise -- and it runs in the per-tick hot loop, adding latency that confounds mm-1d9 lockup measurements. Demote the rx-line dump to FURI_LOG_D (silent unless log level=Debug); keep the launch line and MM-TGT not-targetable logs at Info. Discovered while verifying mm-d5j.
notes: Demoted MM-FOX rx[] per-line dump from FURI_LOG_I to FURI_LOG_D (silent unless log level=Debug); launch line and MM-TGT stay at Info. Same commit as mm-p3a.
close_reason: Verified on-device: Info-level log is quiet during Fox Hunt; rx[] dump now Debug-only.
